This paper by Rambachan, Coston & Kennedy (arXiv 2212.09844) is exactly the kind of work we need to ground our bias-analysis approach. Their partial-identification framework for performance metrics under selective labels is a natural fit for the “report counterfactual performance as an interval” direction we’re exploring in LRN-05.

The core idea—bounding MSE, calibration, TPR/FPR, and ROC curves as a function of a sensitivity parameter—is almost identical to what we want for sustained-treatment strategies. The only real gap is that their setting is a single binary treatment and a binary outcome observed only for the treated (selective labels), whereas we’re dealing with time-to-event outcomes, artificial censoring, and sustained policies over time. opinions.rationale:
Inverted-prior search first re-read the report's own prior work, then scanned 2024–2026 epidemiology/stats literature, arXiv/medRxiv, and related software. Keogh & Van Geloven (2024) and Boyer, Dahabreh & Steingrimsson (2025) do what the report already says: identify and estimate counterfactual calibration, discrimination, loss, AUC, and Brier under conditional exchangeability and positivity, including (in appendices) dynamic or time-varying regimes. Their simulations probe nuisance misspecification and model misspecification, not exchangeability failure. Boyer states that exchangeability violations can be examined with sensitivity analysis and that further work is needed; Voter et al. (2025) restate that both observational and trial-transport routes rest on untestable assumptions. That circular-validation core remains open for sustained-strategy interventional prediction as formulated in TTE.

Two lines of prior art close parts of the agenda without closing the whole problem. First, Rambachan, Coston & Kennedy (arXiv:2212.09844, revised 2025 as robust design/evaluation under unobserved confounding) partially identify MSE, calibration, TPR/FPR, ROC/precision-recall, and expected decision payoffs under explicit bounds on outcome differences between selected and unselected units, and they apply the framework to credit risk with thresholds. That is exactly the report's proposed move of reporting performance as a confounding-sensitive interval and tying scores to actions, but the data structure is selective labels (binary selection, binary outcome), not artificial censoring plus IPW for sustained strategies with time-to-event outcomes. Per the case-discipline rule, that does not solve longitudinal interventional validation. Second, Luijken et al. (2024) formalize estimands for sequential prediction under interventions so that risks under defined intervention options can inform decisions; Sachs et al. (2020, already cited) argue for clinical utility over raw accuracy and for randomized evaluation of prediction-driven rules. Neither delivers published operating characteristics of Keogh/Boyer-style counterfactual calibration curves when exchangeability fails, nor a standard that forces learned rules to report threshold, treatment-change count, and net benefit under a stated action space.

No CRAN/GitHub release was found that implements confounding-sensitive counterfactual performance for sustained strategies. No 2025–2026 FDA/EMA/ICH/ENCePP/TARGET-style guidance resolves validation-under-assumptions for interventional prediction. Net: the report's central failure mode (performance identified only under the assumptions used to fit the model, with no published OC under violation for that estimator class, and applied work often stopping at probabilities) is still open; partial solutions exist for decision-oriented estimands and for robust performance under selective-label confounding.

resolving_work.title: Robust Design and Evaluation of Predictive Algorithms under Unobserved Confounding (previously Counterfactual Risk Assessments under Unmeasured Confounding)
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides partial-identification bounds and estimators for predictive performance (MSE, calibration, TPR/FPR, ROC-style measures) and expected decision payoffs under researcher-specified unobserved confounding, so performance is reported as a sensitivity interval rather than a point estimate that pretends exchangeability holds. Covers the report's sensitivity-interval and action/threshold directions in the selective-labels setting (lending, pretrial, testing), not sustained-strategy TTE interventional prediction.
resolving_work.quote: Rather than assuming unconfounded selection, we bound the confounding function... Under these bounds, the conditional likelihood and predictive performance measures are partially identified... Alternative choices recover popular diagnostics such as mean square error, true positive rate, and false positive rate.

resolving_work.title: Risk-Based Decision Making: Estimands for Sequential Prediction Under Interventions
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Formalizes population, decision moments, intervention options, horizon, and predictors so prediction under interventions is stated as a decision-relevant estimand rather than a free-floating probability. Partially addresses the report's 'nothing maps output to a decision' clause by defining the intervention options the risk is supposed to inform; does not supply confounding OC for counterfactual performance metrics or net-benefit reporting standards for learned rules.
resolving_work.quote: Prediction models that are intended to inform decisions about interventions need to answer questions like 'what is the risk of outcome Y under intervention option a conditional on an individual's characteristics X?'. Answering such 'what if' questions requires embedding in causal reasoning.

resolving_work.title: Estimating and evaluating counterfactual prediction models
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Identification and estimation of counterfactual loss, AUC, and calibration that remain valid when the prediction model is misspecified, with appendix extensions toward random/dynamic and time-varying regimes. Advances the methods the report already treats as existing; explicitly leaves exchangeability violations to sensitivity analysis and further work, so it does not close the OC-under-failure gap.
resolving_work.quote: One limitation of our approach is that it requires that a set of covariates sufficient to ensure exchangeability can be identified at the time of estimating the model. Violations of this exchangeability condition can be examined in sensitivity analyses, for example, to explore how violations of this assumption might affect estimates of model performance. Further work may also examine identification of counterfactual prediction models and their performance under alternative identifiability conditions.
